result.decision_rationale: R14-F1 is fixed. The candidate refused the restored dirty pair when staging had observed the replacement’s clean receipt. Stable external copies kept their expected behavior, and publisher rollback restored both files. The required gate passed at the reviewed commit. The retained production DLL matches the binary covered by the four-loader static audit.

The focused records show the defect on 166fbb9 and five passing checks on 41d3a48. Gate log lines 177–190 independently confirm mixed-pair refusal, stable receiptless staging during unrelated sibling changes, refusal after an absent receipt returned, and publisher rollback.

Its ZIP SHA-256 is 8f757331b42ad157939108702fb59c8c9aae031d0416ee271ac792a0aaa4d344 and its receipt SHA-256 is ba8e64d33d79ff474f8675d31c696d41c6da33f79111e6c6e208587a6994e2c8. source_inspection_only: The staging helper reads the receipt bytes from the handle whose identity it recorded. It checks both external names at selection, after copying and before returning qualification. The external handles share delete access, and build-owned reads use the canonical publication lock.

Git showed identical material build inputs and standalone validation code at the retained producer and the reviewed commit. prior_finding_assessments.rationale: On 166fbb9, the fixture recorded the original ZIP identity and the temporary pair’s clean receipt identity, then returned frozen-candidate after the dirty pair was restored. On the corrected code, the same restoration made the receipt path identify a different file from the opened receipt. The helper refused it at that comparison. The candidate gate also showed that the stable clean pair qualified and the stable dirty pair failed for dirty provenance.
